messages:
sam (eng-arch): Hey team — follow-up from the private control plane spike: we need to land on a minimal-trust handshake for air-gapped customers. Goal: outbound-only from customer -> our relays, short-lived creds, no inbound peering. Thoughts?

mikhail (eng-security): I think outbound-only + mTLS with attestation gives a good balance. Customer agent establishes TLS to relay, we verify cert + attestation blob. Keep PKI short-lived.

tara (eng-runtime): Agree on outbound. Question: who rotates certs? customer or us? Ops burden differs a lot.

jess (infra): We should support two modes: 1) customer-managed certs (for on-prem HSM/KMS), 2) Redwood-issued ephemeral certs via CSR over the same outbound channel. Both doable but different threat models.

mikhail (eng-security): Right. For Redwood-issued, we can do a CSR flow over the tunnel: agent -> relay -> control plane CA service. Response: signed leaf. Agent stores in local keystore. Rotation policy: default 24h for leaf, 7d for intermediate.

sam (eng-arch): Does that require inbound connectivity from our CA to the customer? Trying to avoid that. CSR over the established outbound tunnel keeps barriers low.

mikhail (eng-security): Exactly. No inbound needed. But we must protect CA signing endpoint and audit every CSR. Also require attestation signed by node TPM for higher assurance (optional).

tara (eng-runtime): Implementation notes: connector agent will maintain a single long-lived control channel to a regional relay pool. Inside that channel we multiplex CSR requests, health checks, metrics streams. Should be resilient to NAT/timeouts.

jess (infra): For NAT traversal, we'll use long polling + periodic keepalive. Relay pool must have sticky session pinning to avoid excessive reconnect churn. Also autoscale relays by agent count.

sam (eng-arch): What about fallback when relay unreachable? Customer apps must still be able to talk to local inference nodes. We need graceful degrade to local-only mode.

tara (eng-runtime): Local failover is doable. Agent exposes a localhost proxy that flips routing when handshake absent. But that also means less observability for us — must emit explicit telemetry when in degraded mode.

mikhail (eng-security): Audit & revocation: if a customer key is compromised, ops needs to revoke quickly. We should support short CRLs and a push-style revocation over the control channel. Revocation list size should stay small.

sam (eng-arch): Operationally, how to test this? Looking for an e2e plan that covers onboarding, cert rotation, revocation, and full airgap install.

jess (infra): Proposal: canary on 2 customers in non-prod. Steps: (1) deploy agent vX with CSR flow + local proxy; (2) route to staging relays; (3) simulate relay outage and see failover; (4) rotate leaf certs; (5) trigger revocation.

tara (eng-runtime): Add chaos test for NAT flapping and for relay region failover. Also include a perf run: measure latency added by relay and cert exchange time.

mikhail (eng-security): Also do a threat-model review before canary. Document assumptions: attacker cannot intercept outbound TLS to relay; TPM attestation optional for high-security customers.

sam (eng-arch): Good checklist. One more: key storage options for customers. We need clear docs for "customer-managed KMS" vs "agent keystore".

jess (infra): I can draft onboarding doc. Quick snippet for CSR-over-tunnel we plan to support:

infra-bot: Deploy request created: canary-controlplane-handshake - env: staging - assignees: jess, tara

jess (infra): sample CSR flow (pseudo):
```
# agent -> relay (open channel)
POST /v1/csr/proxy HTTP/1.1
Host: relay.redwood.internal
Body: {"csr": "---BEGIN CSR---..."}

# relay forwards to CA service, returns signed cert
```

mikhail (eng-security): That looks right. Add HSM-backed sign for enterprise customers. Also log CSR metadata to audit pipeline.

tara (eng-runtime): Flag: performance optimization — cache signed certs per agent until expiry to avoid repeat CSR storms on reconnect.

sam (eng-arch): OK. Action items: (1) mikhail — write threat model & rotation policy doc; (2) jess — draft onboarding + CSR flow + run canary deploy; (3) tara — change agent to multiplex CSR and expose local proxy; (4) infra-bot ticket created for canary.

jess (infra): I'll post PRs for docs and a canary runbook.

mikhail (eng-security): I'll post the threat model today.

tara (eng-runtime): I'll prototype multiplexing this week.

sam (eng-arch): Thanks. Quick question for later: do we allow customer-initiated revocation via their KMS webhooks? We should design webhook auth carefully.

mikhail (eng-security): Prefer signed webhooks with mutual TLS and replay protection. We'll follow up in a separate thread.

sam (eng-arch): Sweet. That should keep this thread focused. :thumbsup:
